name: The Unbricked Doorway

detectability.signature: A rectangular absence of universe edged in actinic discharge; gravimetric and magnetic signatures contradict each other hourly

proximity: Long-range sensors resolve the doorway as a flat black rectangle that casts no shadow
Approach triggers cascading navigation contradictions across every sensor band
contact: Crossing the frame transits a ship to an unchartable elsewhere within seconds
Matter touching the frame's edge is shaved away cleanly into the adjacent dimension
prolonged_exposure: Sustained presence within a light-hour invites visitors: objects arriving unbidden from the far side
Local spacetime begins to accrete new volumes built in unfamiliar architectural styles

phenomena: Ships exiting at different locations than entered, or never exiting
Visible distortion of starfield around the frame
Objects appearing larger or smaller than they are near the threshold
opportunities: Communication with other dimensions or times
known_incidents: The exploration cruiser First Course passed through in 2352 and transmitted eleven years of coherent logs over the following week, from no fixed direction
During the great pulse of 2399 a sister-frame opened briefly above the colony Meridian's Rest; nothing crossed, but every clock on the planet lost nine minutes
description: Hanging in interstellar dark is a rectangle of sheer absence, nine-tenths of an astronomical unit tall, framed in seething actinic light as if the universe had left an archway unfinished and unbricked. The frame's proportions are uncomfortably close to monumental architecture, scaled for no species anyone has met. Through the opening there are structures, colonnades, stairs, distances, that no telescope can reconcile.

The Doorway pulses at wildly irregular intervals, sometimes dormant for months, sometimes cycling daily, and each opening rearranges whatever can be glimpsed beyond. Ships drawn across the threshold have never returned physically, though several have sent messages afterward. The frame's edges are lethally precise: hulls touching them lose exactly what touched, and nothing more.

It announced itself with the loss of the cruiser First Course, whose eleven years of subsequent transmissions remain the most studied corpus in the field. Xenologists divide their time between arguing that the far side is a place and insisting it is a machine. Cults have formed around it; most were disappointed by the Doorway's perfect indifference.

Admiralties enforce an exclusion volume measured in light-days, revised upward after every large pulse. Listening stations keep vigil for the next opening, and for whatever watches back through it. Travelers are advised that the shortest path between two points is never through the Doorway.
